keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 619-621 for a state Cliopatria lacks: the infobox territory 'Henan/Northern Jiangsu/Northern Anhui'. The article names Henan places (Liyang, Yin Prefecture); Hubei and southern Shandong are not given. No area on the page. The extent is a province span, not a boundary; the Tang took the cities 'one by one' in 620-621.

ledger.note: 619: Wang Shichong founds the Zheng at Luoyang. 'In summer 619,' he had Yang Tong yield the throne and established 'a new state of Zheng'; he had seized power at Luoyang after killing Lu Chu and defeated Li Mi at Yanshi in fall 618.

region.text: Luoyang and the Zheng cities Li Shimin took one by one

ledger.note: 620: the Tang besiege Luoyang. 'Li Shimin besieged Luoyang from fall 620 and into spring 621' and 'captured Zheng cities one by one'.
621: Wang surrenders after Hulao. 'Dou Jiande advanced to Hulao in summer 621,' where Li Shimin defeated and captured him; Wang then surrendered.

ledger.note: 621: the Zheng ends. Wang Shichong surrendered after Dou Jiande's capture (summer 621) and died c. August 621; Zheng and Xia were annexed by the Tang (Transition page).

wars.name: Tang campaign against Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong

zones.text: Luoyang, Hulao and the Zheng cities

wars.outcome: Tang victory at Hulao in summer 621; Zheng and Xia annexed.
wars.note: The same war is listed in the Dou Jiande dossier.

certainty.note: The extent is the infobox's province span; no boundary is given.

sources.note: The Zheng 619-621 in the list of rival regimes; Luoyang as its capital.

notes: REBEL STATE for the successor of Yang Tong's Sui at Luoyang. The Sui dossier names this slug in its 619 dissolve. The page gives no month for the founding ('summer 619') or the surrender; the extent is the infobox span read as Henan plus the Yangtze-Huai strip's Jiangsu and Anhui parts. Wang Shichong asked Dou Jiande for aid in 621. Tang text names (ea-04) 'Wang Shichong (Zheng)' should use this slug.
